content.comment_body: I am planning a system to receive temperature data from several remote locations onto a computer. At every site, I install a [product_name] controller with a temperature sensor. I want to know how many [product_name] controllers can be connected to send data to the computer from all sites. Regards, [user_name]
What do you mean exactly by "different sites"?

Hello, I suggest using [product_name] [version_no] with a connection to AWS cloud. Each location will require a [product_name] [version_no] and Internet access, either through an existing network or a 4G/LTE router with LAN. Configure each [product_name] to communicate with your AWS account. If several [product_name] units upload data to the same AWS account, use unique IoT names for each device, which can be incorporated into the dashboard. You can view all site data in a single AWS dashboard once configured. Hope this is helpful.

For illustration, imagine having clients across the country and sampling data like room temperature from each system. For every client, a [product_name] controller is installed to collect the data. I need to understand the maximum number of [product_name] units that can be installed at client locations and monitored. Regards, [user_name]
How many [product_name] controllers are you planning to connect?
A single [product_name] [article_no] can connect with a maximum of 16 other [product_name] units, 8 of which are static connections and 8 are dynamic.
With 80 [product_name] controllers, you will need to assign certain units as data collectors, which aggregate data from others before transferring it to a main [product_name].

For 80 [product_name] controllers, a similar approach where some devices act as data collectors before forwarding data to a main unit would be needed. If I choose a main controller like [product_name] [version_no], or is there another recommendation? Is it possible to manage 80 [product_name] units this way? Regards, [user_name]

Yes, this is the only feasible solution. However, whether it functions reliably with 80 [product_name] units isn't certain—I haven't worked on a project with this scale. These are just theoretical considerations.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are investigating how scalable [product_name] controllers are for remote data collection from multiple locations. There's a notable gap in clear information about how many [product_name] devices can be interconnected and centrally managed. The discussion highlights hardware limitations in direct networking, uncertainties about integrating higher-level controllers, and alternatives like cloud-based aggregation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user aims to connect up to 80 [product_name] controllers from distinct sites to a central system, hoping for straightforward data aggregation and minimal complexity in infrastructure setup.
